glosses: The condition of being held in a state between two or more forces, which are acting in opposition to each other.

examples.text: My tensions with Eric over his alleged past actions have been fully resolved.

glosses: A psychological state of being tense.
A feeling of nervousness, excitement, or fear that is created in a movie, book, etc.; suspense.
The state of an elastic object which is stretched in a way which increases its length.

A force transmitted through a rope, string, cable, or similar object (used with prepositions on, in, or of, e.g., \"The tension in the cable is 1000 N\", to convey that the same magnitude of force applies to objects attached to both ends).
Voltage.
To place an object in tension, to pull or place strain on.

examples.text: We tensioned the cable until it snapped.

glosses: A specific pitch.
(in the diatonic scale) An interval of a major second.
(in a Gregorian chant) A recitational melody.
The character of a sound, especially the timbre of an instrument or voice.
The pitch of a word's sound that distinguishes a difference in meaning, as for example in Chinese.
A whining style of speaking; a kind of mournful or artificial strain of voice; an affected speaking with a measured rhythm and a regular rise and fall of the voice.

examples.text: Children often read with a tone.

glosses: The manner in which speech or writing is expressed, especially the aspects of diction (word choice), connotation, emotiveness, and register.

examples.text: Their tone was dissatisfied, almost menacing.

glosses: State of mind; temper; mood.

examples.text:
c. 1714 (undated), Henry St John, 1st Viscount Bolingbroke, letter to Alexander Pope
The strange situation I am in and the melancholy state of public affairs, […] drag the mind down […] from a philosophical tone or temper, to the drudgery of private and public business.

glosses: The shade or quality of a colour.

examples.text: We make crude visual distinctions and effectively meaningless categorizations based on average skin tones, such as black or white.

glosses: The favourable effect of a picture produced by the combination of light and shade, or of colours.

examples.text: This picture has tone.

glosses: The definition and firmness of a muscle or organ; see also: tonus.
The state of a living body or of any of its organs or parts in which the functions are healthy and performed with due vigor.
Normal tension or responsiveness to stimuli.
a gun

glosses: The general character, atmosphere, mood, or vibe (of a situation, place, etc.).

examples.text: Her rousing speech gave an upbeat tone to the rest of the evening.

Mr O'Brien confirmed the warning from the council was based on the fact that the structure the mural was painted on was not a temporary one and on the claim that it changes the tone of the street and impacts on the area.

"What struck me most was not necessarily what was said but ... the tone of the room, ... the fear and anxiety that people have for their family members who are currently in the grip of addiction," Green said.

glosses: The quality of being respectable or admirable.

examples.text: "I am going to raise the tone of the business. That's wot I want you for. To raise the tone of the business."

The teaching we have had of late has lowered the tone of Christianity, as the remarks by the two gentlemen who preceded me will attest; and, instead of producing stalwart manhood, it has generated a brood of mountebanks. Give us a pure Gospel or a vacant pulpit!

But for anyone hoping that what proved to be a brief two-way female Tory leadership race might have raised the tone of British politics—currently at an all-time low after the vicious backroom machinations of Brexit referendum—the news wasn't promising.
That story is replicated wherever there is a brightly decorated house and a neighbour who cares about the tone of the street.

glosses: Propiedad de los sonidos que los caracteriza como más agudos o más graves, en función de su frecuencia.

examples.text: Tienes que usar el ecualizador para eliminar esos tonos disonantes.

glosses: Cualidad sonora del habla que depende de la actitud u otros factores de la persona en cuestión.

examples.text: Su tono de voz me dio a entender que estaba enojado.

glosses: Sonido emitido por un teléfono u otro aparato de comunicación como indicación de que la línea telefónica está activa y funcionando, o al momento de presionar una tecla o botón del dispositivo.

examples.text: Levanté el teléfono como de costumbre, ignorando por completo el apagón, pero por supuesto no había tono.

glosses: Conjunto de características de un texto u otra obra, artística o de otro tipo, el cual surge a partir de su modo de redacción o composición en función del contexto o tema que se relacione con tal producción.

examples.text: Ciertas composiciones de Shostakóvich tenían un tono burlón hacia el régimen de gobierno de su momento.

glosses: Implicación respecto a cierta creencia, moral o ideología.

examples.text: La letra de esta canción tiene tonos satánicos.

glosses: Apariencia de un color, por ejemplo su brillo, saturación, contraste, o la combinación de tales cualidades.

examples.text: Muchas prendas con tonos rojizos se han vendido este verano.

glosses: Frecuencia o entonación de una palabra o lema.

examples.text: El idioma chino es conocido por su uso de tonos en cada palabra.

glosses: En una escala musical, la distribución de sus notas.

examples.text: Hay películas cuyas bandas sonoras utilizan tonos poco convencionales de la escala de do, como el eólico, con el objetivo de crear una atmósfera exótica.

glosses: Nombre de una escala musical basado en su nota principal o fundamental.

examples.text: La banda comenzó a interpretar una canción en tono de do sostenido.

glosses: Intervalo musical equivalente a dos semitonos, o a la distancia entre dos notas o teclas adyacentes de un piano.
